title: Optimized flow cytometric protocol for the detection of functional subsets of low frequency antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells
author: Mura, Chaudhury, et al.

steps.title: Place cells on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the cell suspension on ice for 15 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and wash the pellet with cold Flow Buffer.
Centrifuge again at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Stain with activation‑marker antibody
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in CD154‑biotin or CD69‑biotin antibody diluted in Flow Buffer and incubate for 15 minutes at 4 °C (use CD154 for CD4⁺ enrichment, CD69 for CD4⁺/CD8⁺ enrichment).

steps.title: Add anti‑biotin microbeads
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL anti‑biotin microbeads in Flow Buffer to the cell suspension and incubate for 15 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash post‑bead incubation
steps.instruction: Wash cells with cold Flow Buffer and centrifuge at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Surface staining with viability dye
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in surface‑stain antibody cocktail containing a viability dye and incubate for 30 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after surface staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells with cold Flow Buffer and centrifuge at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in fixation/permeabilization solution and incubate for 20 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after fixation
steps.instruction: Wash cells with cold Flow Buffer and centrifuge at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in intracellular stain antibody cocktail and incubate for 30 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Wash cells with cold Flow Buffer and centrifuge at 350 g for 6 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final resuspension for magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 500 µL manual separation buffer.

steps.title: Quantitative data analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the acquired data using FlowJo v10 (Treestar, Ashland, OR); calculate frequencies as percentage of parent populations (e.g., CD4⁺IFN‑γ⁺ as % of CD4⁺ cells) following the gating strategy described (lymphocytes → singlets → viability → CD3 → activation marker → cytokine).

description: Understanding immunity is essential for improving disease intervention strategies or vaccine design. The characterization of lymphocyte subsets participating in immune responses induced by either immunization or infection produces the data that hold the promise to reveal immune mechanisms of protection or pathogenesis. The assessment of cytokines can be done either based on measuring secreted cytokines of bulk stimulated leukocytes (or pre-sorted/enriched cell subsets) by multiplex assays or ELISA, or by measuring the cytokines at the cellular level using gene chip assays, RNAseq, or flow cytometry (cytokine capture assays or intracellular staining). Flow cytometry has been a particularly useful method as it allows the identification and characterization of cell populations involved in an immune response. Characterization of functional cell subsets is accomplished by staining for cell surface markers specific for leukocyte lineages, markers of activation/differentiation, and functional markers such as intracellular detection of cytokines. Unfortunately, the frequency of antigen-specific cells is often at or below the detection threshold of conventional flow cytometry [1]. The technical challenge is to amplify the signal of the antigen-specific cells well above the usual detection threshold. There are several options depending on the source of the samples to reduce the background noise thus allowing rare cell detection: (1) tetramer staining in case where the HLA haplotypes of the donors are known; (2) design flow cytometric panels reserving bright fluorochromes for the identification of the low frequency population(s) and processing/acquiring large sample sizes; (3) design strategies such as extensive cleaning procedures prior to sample acquisition to reduce instrumentation-associated noise and extended flushing of the flow cell between samples to reduce the sample carryover.
